text:
maria: heads up — multiple customers reporting slow responses on /v1/generate around 10:03 UTC. SLO alert fired and p95 looks up compared to baseline

maria: quick numbers from dashboard: p95 ~420ms (was ~120ms), p99 spikes up to 2.3s. Error-rate small but visible latency regressions. dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/rumps

devin: i'm seeing elevated GPU mem usage in pool-rw-3, fragmentation metric climbed sharply. gpu_mem_util 88% -> 96%, gpu_fragmentation ~42% -> ~55% in the same window

alex: runtime logs show allocator OOM warnings then fallbacks to CPU path which blocks token generation. snippets from runtime.log: ```[10:08:37] WARN kv_cache: growth to 1.8GB (threshold 1.2GB) -> triggering growth path
[10:08:38] ERROR allocator: failed to allocate 72MB gpu -> OOM, fragmentation high
[10:08:38] INFO fallback: serving from cpu-cache, increased latency```

tara: Dedicated customers reported bumps too, lower frequency. common pattern: very long concatenated prompts with repeated prefixes — KV cache keeps growing no eviction

maria: any recent config or deploy flips? vikram?

vikram: no model binary changes in last 24h. We did set kv_cache.enabled=true by default in runtime-config v2.14 (rolled 3 days ago). also allocator is cuda-allocator v1.3 (no eager compaction)

devin: hypothesis: kv_cache default growth combined with allocator fragmentation -> OOM -> CPU fallback -> p95/p99 regressions

maria: which nodes showed OOMs? need node ids and process restarts

devin: nodes: pool-rw-3-06, pool-rw-3-07, pool-rw-3-09 — repeated cuda OOM logs and runtime process restarts around 10:09-10:12

sre-bot: incident created INC-197400-1 "p95/p99 regression - GPU memory fragmentation / kv growth" assigned to eng-runtime

alex: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) per-pool runtime-config override to disable kv_cache on affected pool, 2) lightweight routing to smaller model-variant for huge contexts, 3) rolling restart to defrag GPUs

tara: full cluster kv_cache disable would hurt latency for some workloads. prefer targeted per-pool overrides first

maria: agreed. devin, can you apply per-pool override? suggested command:
```
runtime-config set pool:pool-rw-3 kv_cache.enabled=false --expiry 30m
```

devin: applying now
deploy-bot: config-change applied to pool-rw-3 @ 10:31 UTC (runtime-config v2.14 override)
devin: done. also dropped max_concurrency from 32 -> 16 on that pool to reduce concurrent allocations

alex: after override p95 on pool-rw-3 dropped to ~160ms within five minutes. p99 still noisy but trending down

maria: good. next: confirm root cause — why did kv cache grow without bound? check eviction policy & entry TTLs

vikram: config shows kv_cache.eviction_policy=LRU. but streaming/session-created kv entries currently have no TTL. combined with very long sessions and repeated prefixes sessions accumulate large KV sets

alex: allocator is v1.3; v1.4 includes fragmentation mitigation (eager compaction). canarying an allocator bump could help
tara: plan proposals:
- short-term: per-pool kv_cache.max_size=1GB + kv_cache.entry_ttl=60s for high-memory pools; lower concurrency limits where needed
- medium-term: canary allocator upgrade to v1.4 and run synthetic workload to measure fragmentation impact
- long-term: implement smarter KV eviction heuristics that consider token age and session activity, plus default TTL for stream entries

maria: owners? devin (short-term overrides), alex (allocator canary), vikram (eviction design)

devin: will push overrides to two more risky pools and schedule rolling restarts across pool-rw-* tonight 02:00 UTC; monitoring will be active

alex: canary plan: upgrade allocator on pool-canary-1 and run loadgen replicating long-prefix-repeat test. loadgen command i'll use:
```
./tools/loadgen --model model-redwood-large-prod --pattern long-prefix-repeat --qps 50 --duration 30m
```

maria: routing mitigation as well — prefer smaller model variant for requests with context > 8k tokens to avoid huge KV growth on the large model

vikram: i'll add routing rule: if (context_tokens > 8000) route -> model-redwood-large-quant (lower kv footprint)

devin: rolling restart started 02:10 UTC off-peak. tailing logs and metrics now for regressions
sre-bot: scheduled maintenance window 1974038400-1974042000

maria: postmortem artifacts to collect: timeline, p95/p99 by pool & model, allocator logs, kv_cache metrics (entries, size, evictions), applied overrides, impacted customers and tickets
tara: i made temporary dashboards: /d/pools/kv_growth and /d/alloc/fragmentation for the incident. sharing links in the incident doc

alex: after overrides and routing changes we should also default to a non-zero TTL for streaming kv entries in runtime v2.15

vikram: ack — drafting RFC for eviction heuristics + default TTL change (perf vs quality tradeoffs) — ETA 72h

maria: action items recap:
- devin: apply kv_cache.max_size=1GB + entry_ttl=60s to affected pools and lower concurrency where needed (ETA 30m)
- alex: run allocator v1.4 canary + loadgen and report fragmentation delta (ETA 24h)
- vikram: design KV eviction + TTL RFC (ETA 72h)
- tara: assemble incident graphs + customer impact summary (ETA 4h)
- maria: coordinate customer comms/update support tickets (ETA 1h)

sre-bot: INC-197400-1 status: mitigated (kv_cache override + routing) assigned -> eng-runtime
devin: monitoring shows p95 near baseline across most pools with overrides in place; keeping overrides for 2h to ensure stability

maria: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for updates. if regressions recur after reverting overrides we escalate allocator patch earlier and consider rolling TTL change sooner :thumbsup:
